question: Should exact requester consumption of descendant fallback output count as durable descendant delivery proof even when the final outward cron delivery later fails?
rationale: The PR deliberately changes the delivery boundary from visible descendant delivery to requester consumption for matched rows, which affects retry/finalization semantics and cannot be settled by tests alone.

options.title: Accept after proof and dedupe fix
options.body: Keep the requester-consumed delivery boundary, but require the generation-aware dedupe repair plus redacted real runtime or SQLite restore proof before merge.

options.title: Credit only after outward delivery
options.body: Require cron requester-consumption credit to happen only after the requester result is successfully delivered outward, preserving stronger visible-delivery semantics.

options.title: Defer to durable inbox design
options.body: Pause this PR and handle the scenario in the broader durable subagent completion inbox/spool work instead of adding a separate requester-consumption boundary now.

recommendation.title: Accept after proof and dedupe fix
recommendation.body: Keep the requester-consumed delivery boundary, but require the generation-aware dedupe repair plus redacted real runtime or SQLite restore proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is closest to the deterministic subagent announce/descendant gating behavior introduced in the merged feature history.
